entries.english:
Additional plaintiff/intervener: Count Wolfgang zu Castell of Castell and Remlingen. Additional defendant/intervener: Albrecht Christoph von Rosenberg of Rosenberg and Waldmannshofen, councilor and collector of the Odenwald knightly canton; also intervening were Hans Sigmund Zollner von und zu Hallburg and Hans Georg von Fronhofen.
Plaintiff’s attorney: Lic. Peter Paul Steurnagel (1603). Defendant’s attorneys: (Dr. Johann Melchior) Weißenberger (1604); Dr. Johann Gödelmann (1604); Dr. Christodorus Engelhardt (1604); Dr. Georg Amandus Wolf (1605); Dr. Johann Melchior Reinhardt (1606).
Subject (contemporary): summons to appear so that guardians may be appointed.
Subject (modern): Assumption of guardianship over the minor son of the Castellian feudal tenant Wilhelm von Vestenberg. After Wilhelm’s death, the count considered his fief at and around Burghaslach endangered and took interim administration of it. In the absence of agnatic relatives, he asked the defendants, as the nearest cognatic relatives, to assume guardianship of the minor Adam von Vestenberg. They refused, citing private and official business, litigation, and other guardianships; Albrecht Christoph von Rosenberg also cited a disagreement with the widow Margaretha Agatha Zollner von Hallburg. The intervener, the ward’s brother-in-law, had been temporarily entrusted with guardianship administration by the directors, captains, and councilors of the Franconian Imperial Knighthood and opposed the count’s involvement. The count accused him of damaging the fief and oppressing Vestenberg’s subjects. On 25 September 1606 the defendants were released from the summons.
Proceedings: Imperial Chamber Court, 1604–1607 (record dates also given as 1604–1606).
Contains: Reconciliation oath of the intervener, arrested in 1604 for threatening and injuring Vestenberg subjects at Burghaslach (item 17); excerpt from the knightly ordinance concerning assistance to widows and orphans (no. 20).

Process register: proceedings began in 1604.
